messages:
Alice Park: :rotating_light: multiple customers hitting 502/504 from hosted inference in eu-central-1, started ~05:12 UTC. high sev. customers: ACME (acct: acme-prod), NimbusAI. getting lots of escalations to support.
Ben Liu: Oncall - looking. Any pattern by AZ/region? request ids / example timestamps?
Alice Park: seems concentrated in eu-central-1.az2. Support dug up a few sample errors from ACME:
Support Bot: "curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx' -d '{\"input\":\"hi\"}'" returns 502 with body: "{\"error\":\"gateway_timeout\",\"code\":502,\"correlation_id\":\"c-id-20260315-0728\"}"
Alice Park: also seeing increased p50/p95 latency on the gateway for the same region: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/latency/eu-central-1
Carla Gomez: net-eng - I see packet loss spikes on the egress path from eu-central-1.az2 to transit-provider-2 around 05:10-05:40 UTC. graphs: tx drops and retransmits. suspect provider-level micro-loss. ping/traceroute shows intermittent TTL drops.
Nate R: SRE - can you paste the traceroute? also any BGP flaps? we should check bgp sessions with provider.
Carla Gomez: traceroute to transit provider edge (one sample):
```
traceroute to 203.0.113.12 (203.0.113.12), 30 hops max
 1  10.16.0.1 (10.16.0.1)  0.45 ms  0.40 ms  0.39 ms
 2  198.51.100.2 (198.51.100.2)  2.2 ms  2.1 ms  2.0 ms
 3  198.51.200.7 (198.51.200.7)  18.9 ms  20.1 ms  180.2 ms  <-- intermittent jump
 4  203.0.113.12 (203.0.113.12)  21.5 ms  22.0 ms  21.8 ms
```
Carla Gomez: see that hop 3 had a big jump in one sample -> correlates with packet loss/retransmits.
Sasha Ivanov: Platform - are we routing traffic from gateway to runtime in the same AZ, or crossing AZs? want to understand blast radius.
Ben Liu: Gateway forwards to runtime endpoints in same AZ by default (affinity) to keep latency down. if az2 runtime path is flaky, traffic could time out waiting for connection to local runtime.
Nate R: Confirmed in logs: gateway-to-runtime connection resets and ECONNRESET. sample gateway log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T05:15:08Z] gateway request_id=c-id-20260315-0728 route=eu-central-1.az2 -> runtime connection reset after 10s
[2026-03-15T05:16:12Z] gateway request_id=c-id-20260315-0739 error=upstream_timeout
```
Alice Park: customers are angry, ACME says they hit multiple 502s during a demo. CS wants ETA and mitigation now.
Ben Liu: Immediate mitigations we can try:
- Shift gateway routing weight away from eu-central-1.az2 to az1/az3 for affected customers.
- Temporarily mark runtimes in az2 as draining for hosted inference traffic.
- Ask transit provider for an emergency investigation (open ticket + provide pcap/flow samples).
Carla Gomez: I'll open provider ticket now. Transit Ops, assigning to you for BGP/peering checks.
Transit Ops: Acked. I see minor BGP route churn around 05:09-05:18 UTC on session with transit-provider-2. opening internal ticket with provider with logs and pcap. ticket ref: TP-87612.
Sasha Ivanov: I'll patch routing policy to add weighted fallback for 15m and increase connection timeout thresholds at gateway to avoid spurious 502s while we mitigate. rolling change now.
Infra Bot: Deployment scheduled: change-id=chg-3091, target=gateway-routing, rollout=canary->all, owner=Sasha Ivanov
Ben Liu: Also enable cross-AZ failover for these customers to reduce dependency on az2. I'll add a temporary override for accounts acme-prod and nimbusai.
Alice Park: Support -> customers updated: ACME notified with suggested workaround: retry with exponential backoff and fallback to dedicated capacity if urgent. CS asked for status updates every 10m.
Nate R: After routing change, p50/p95 latency improved at 05:28 UTC for eu-central-1 overall. however some in-flight requests still saw 502s due to existing connections to runtimes in az2.
Support Bot: sample correlation ids to track: c-id-20260315-0728, c-id-20260315-0739, c-id-20260315-0802
Carla Gomez: Provider responded: they saw microbursts on one of their interconnects, confirmed packet loss and are applying mitigations on their side. will keep open until stable.
Ben Liu: For postmortem action items:
- (Net) collect pcap/flow for 05:00-06:00 and hand to provider.
- (SRE) add healthcheck to detect sustained packet loss on runtime ingress and mark AZ unhealthy earlier.
- (Platform) make cross-AZ fallback default for critical accounts or SLO-sensitive traffic.
- (Support) prepare templated customer comms for network-induced 5xx.
Alice Park: CS: I'll prepare comms and include compensation options if this affected SLAs for paying customers.
Nate R: Will follow up with a short incident report after we confirm provider fix and ensure no residual error rate. tagging @carla and @sasha for final confirmation before close.
Carla Gomez: Provider applied changes at 05:42 UTC; packet loss dropped to baseline by 05:50 UTC. monitoring shows normal retransmit rates afterwards.
Sasha Ivanov: rollout changelog: gateway timeout extended + routing weights adjusted, rolled back to normal at 06:10 UTC after stability window.
Alice Park: Customer updates: ACME acknowledged mitigation and will rerun their demo tomorrow. CS asked for incident summary and credits. Marking incident: RESOLVED (root cause: transit provider micro-loss affecting eu-central-1.az2 egress). :white_check_mark:
Support Bot: Incident closed in PagerDuty: PD-5231. Postmortem assigned to Nate R (owner) and due in 72h.
Ben Liu: Thanks everyone. small follow-ups will be tracked in the postmortem. :thumbsup:
